archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm distributor)
archetype.definition: An 11th-year timing passer who wins from the pocket with accuracy over the short and intermediate middle rather than with arm-strength shots or his legs, and who runs mainly to escape trouble.

report.headline: Efficient, accurate and Lamb-centric, with some red-zone and sack luck mixed in
report.take:
Prescott is the same quarterback he has been for a decade. He gets the ball out in about 2.7-2.8 seconds, throws to an average depth around 7.5-8.5 yards, and lives on completion percentage and placement rather than chunk plays. What has changed this year is the polish. His 6.3 CPOE ranks 5th of 42, his 0.312 EPA per dropback ranks 6th, and his 11.3% bad-throw rate lines up with the 11.2% and 11.5% he posted in 2025 and 2023. The accuracy is real and has been for three of his last four seasons. The outlier is 2024.

The engine is CeeDee Lamb and the 10-19 yard window. Lamb has 47 of the 150 targets, about 31%, at 0.886 EPA per target. Nobody else is above 0.363. On intermediate throws Prescott is at 0.733 EPA with four touchdowns on 32 attempts, and over the middle he is completing 79.2% with four scores on 24 throws. The other driver is his own defense. Dallas ranks 31st in defensive EPA and dead last against the pass, so every game has turned into a shootout. All four went over the total, with a combined 58.5 points per game. That has pushed his volume from 34 attempts to 45 by Week 4.

The rate stats are kinder than the per-attempt production. His 7.1 yards per attempt ranks only 22nd. A heavy screen and behind-the-line diet drags the passing game: 32 attempts at -0.352 EPA, more than a fifth of his throws. The EPA total is propped up by finishing. He has seven touchdowns on 23 red-zone attempts while completing just 56.5% there. Ball security has also been unusually clean: one interception, and an 11.5% pressure-to-sack rate. His career says both will drift. He finished 51st of 65 in interceptions last year and 47th of 67 in 2023, and his pressure-to-sack rate has mostly sat between 19% and 35%.

The outlook is still strong, because the parts that hold up over time are the parts doing most of the work: accuracy, the Lamb connection, and a defense that forces him to throw. Expect the touchdown rate to cool and a few more sacks and picks to show up. The yardage should stay high as long as Dallas keeps giving up 28 points a game.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy over the middle
strengths.body: The 10-19 yard throws are where he does the most damage, with high success and touchdowns, and the middle of the field has been his most accurate area. This is timing and placement rather than arm talent. His bad-throw rate matches his best recent seasons, so this should hold.

strengths.title: Lamb as a reliable answer
strengths.body: Lamb is drawing almost a third of the targets and turning them into far more value than anyone else on the roster. Leaning this hard on one receiver works because the efficiency is extraordinary. It also gives Prescott a dependable read on third down, where he is converting half his chances.

strengths.title: Shootout volume built into the roster
strengths.body: Dallas's pass defense ranks last and gives up explosive passes at the league's highest rate. That keeps Prescott throwing in every game, and his attempts and yards climbed to season highs in Week 4. As long as the defense stays this bad, his volume floor is high.

concerns.title: Screen game is dead weight
concerns.body: More than a fifth of his attempts go behind the line, and they are losing value at a heavy rate with negative CPOE. This is a scheme choice, not a flaw in his game. It does explain why his yards per attempt lags well behind his EPA rank.

concerns.title: Turnover and sack luck due to fade
concerns.body: One interception and a pressure-to-sack rate near the top of the league are both better than he has ever sustained. Last season he ranked near the bottom in interceptions with a pressure-to-sack rate roughly double this year's. Expect both numbers to drift back toward his norms.

concerns.title: Red-zone TD rate on thin accuracy
concerns.body: Seven touchdowns on 23 red-zone throws is a finishing rate that rarely holds, especially when he completes only about half of those passes. The scoring total will likely slow even if the offense keeps moving.

trend.note: His per-game passing EPA has stayed in a 9.8-15.1 band. Volume has climbed from 34 attempts to 45, while accuracy slipped a bit after a near-perfect Week 2, including a 22.5% bad-throw game against Baltimore.

nextGame.headline: A stout run defense with a thin secondary, and a lead may cap volume
nextGame.body:
Tampa Bay's defense is good where Dallas is weakest. It ranks 3rd against the run, and Dallas's ground game already rates below average, so the offense will run through Prescott again. The Bucs' pass defense is only middle of the pack, though, and it barely pressures the quarterback. It ranks 29th in hit rate and 25th in sack rate, which suits a rhythm passer who has been pressured on just 17% of dropbacks. The catch is game script. Tampa's offense ranks last in EPA, and Prescott has thrown only seven passes this year while leading by nine or more.

Availability matters on both sides. Tampa is without Baker Mayfield, who played 98% of snaps, which makes a comfortable Dallas lead more likely and could cut Prescott's attempts. The Bucs are also missing safety Antoine Winfield Jr. and corner Benjamin Morrison, and linebacker Josiah Trotter (86% of snaps) is questionable. All three bear directly on the intermediate middle, where Prescott and Lamb do their best work. For Dallas, guard Tyler Smith was limited in practice off IR with a return date of game day. He has not played this season, and his return would only firm up a pocket that has already held up. This is also a short week, on four days' rest.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against a depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: With Winfield and Morrison out and Trotter questionable, Tampa's coverage over the middle is thinner than its overall pass-defense rank suggests. That is exactly where Prescott has been most efficient.

keyMatchups.title: Run game likely stalls again
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's run defense is among the league's best, and Dallas's rushing EPA is already negative. Expect early downs to tilt toward the pass. That supports his volume even with a lead.

keyMatchups.title: Backup-QB Bucs and game script
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's offense is the league's worst even before losing its starter. If Dallas jumps ahead, Prescott's attempts may fall well short of the 45 he threw in Houston.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dallas builds an early lead and leans conservative, or Tampa's backup quarterback finds enough against the league's worst pass defense to keep Prescott throwing into the second half.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy, the Lamb connection and the shootout volume are all durable, so a top-10 efficiency season is realistic. He has already produced that kind of season in 2023 with near-identical bad-throw numbers. What should come back down is the red-zone touchdown rate, the single interception and the unusually low sack rate under pressure. Expect touchdowns to settle somewhat below his current pace, more picks than one every 150 throws, and yards per game holding in the mid-to-high 200s while the defense keeps forcing him to pass.

The secondary targets matter more over a full season. Pickens is the only other receiver producing well, and if defenses take Lamb away, the efficiency of Flournoy, Ferguson and Williams would drag the rate stats toward his 2025 level.
swingFactors: Whether Dallas's last-ranked pass defense improves (less shootout volume)
Tyler Smith's return to the interior line

bets.reason: All four Dallas games went over, but Tampa brings the league's worst offense without its starting quarterback plus a top-5 defense. This is a far less explosive pairing than Washington, Baltimore or Houston.

Dallas's defense ranks 31st in EPA and last against the pass, and only one of its four games was decided by more than nine points. Laying nearly ten with a defense that gives up about 28 a game asks a lot, even against a backup quarterback.

A likely Dallas lead plus a Tampa defense that limits explosive passes (8th) points to fewer and shorter dropbacks than the 40-45 attempt shootouts of the last two weeks. The thin Tampa secondary keeps this a lean rather than a strong play.

confidence.note: Four-game sample, but the accuracy profile matches a long career baseline; TD and sack rates are the shaky parts.
